## What's in this World Cup dataset

The data (Postgres "World Cup Core") covers **the 2018 and 2022 FIFA World Cups** in detail. It's organized around these entities:

**Core tournament structure**
- **tournaments** – 2018 & 2022, host country, dates, champion/runner-up
- **matches** – every match with stage (group, round of 16, quarter/semi-final, third place, final), teams, scores, extra time/penalties, attendance, venue
- **venues** – stadiums, cities, capacities
- **tournament_teams** – each team's participation per tournament (group, final rank, whether they reached the knockout stage)

**Teams & players**
- **teams** / **countries** / **confederations** – team identities linked to country and confederation (UEFA, CONMEBOL, CAF, AFC, CONCACAF)
- **players** – name, position, date of birth, national team
- **squad_members** – tournament rosters (shirt numbers, squad positions)

**Match events**
- **goals** – scorer, assist, minute, goal type (open play, penalty, own goal, header, free kick), running score
- **disciplinary_events** – cards (yellow seen so far), minute, reason
- **match_team_statistics** – per-team per-match stats: possession, shots, shots on target, corners, fouls, offsides, passing, expected goals

**Pre-built convenience views**
- **v_match_results** – match results with team/venue names already joined in (easier than the raw matches table)
- **v_player_goal_totals** – goals, penalties, own goals and first-goal minute per player per tournament
- **v_seeded_team_performance** – team-level summary per tournament (wins, goals for/against, possession, shots, xG, attendance)

**What you can analyze with this:** tournament and match results, top scorers and assist leaders, disciplinary records, team performance by confederation, shooting/possession efficiency, squad composition, venue attendance patterns — all comparable across the 2018 and 2022 tournaments. Note the data does not extend to any other World Cup years.
